datadog_dashboard.default_timeframe.from: The start of the default time range for the dashboard, in epoch milliseconds.
datadog_dashboard.default_timeframe.to: The end time of the default time range for the dashboard, expressed as a Unix timestamp.
datadog_dashboard.default_timeframe.type: The type of default timeframe for the dashboard, indicating whether it is a rolling time window or a fixed date range (e.g., 'rolling' or 'fixed').
datadog_dashboard.tabs.name: The name of the tab, which serves as its title. The name must be between 1 and 100 characters.
datadog_dashboard.tabs.widget_ids: The list of widget IDs contained within this tab.
datadog_dashboard.template_variable_presets.name: The name of the template variable preset.
datadog_dashboard.template_variable_presets.template_varia: List of template variable assignments for this preset. Each object defines a template variable name and the value to apply when the preset is selected.
The name of the template variable to override, matching a template variable defined on the dashboard.
The value to assign to the template variable when this preset is applied.
The list of values assigned to the template variable when this preset is applied.
datadog_dashboard.template_variables.available_values: List of values available for selection for this template variable. If not specified, all possible values are shown in the dropdown.
datadog_dashboard.template_variables.default: The default value assigned to the template variable when the dashboard is loaded. This value is used unless the viewer changes it.
datadog_dashboard.template_variables.defaults: Default value(s) used for this template variable when the dashboard is loaded. Provide a list of strings to support multi-select variables.
datadog_dashboard.template_variables.name: The name of the template variable, used to reference it in dashboard queries and widgets.
datadog_dashboard.template_variables.prefix: The prefix used to filter the available values for the template variable, typically a tag key followed by a colon (e.g., 'env:').
datadog_dashboard.widgets.definition: The definition block that specifies the configuration for the widget, including the widget type and type-specific settings (e.g., requests, title, layout). The exact structure varies by widget type.
datadog_dashboard.widgets.layout: Layout of the widget within the dashboard, specifying its position and size on the grid.
datadog_dashboard.widgets.layout.height: The height of the widget in grid units. The minimum allowed value is 0.
datadog_dashboard.widgets.layout.is_column_break: Set to true to treat this widget as a column break, which forces the next widget to start a new column in the structured layout.
datadog_dashboard.widgets.layout.width: The width of the widget in grid units (columns) within the dashboard layout. The minimum allowed value is 0.
datadog_dashboard.widgets.layout.x: The horizontal position (column) of the widget in the dashboard grid. Must be greater than or equal to 0.
datadog_dashboard.widgets.layout.y: The vertical position of the widget on the dashboard grid, measured from the top. The value must be greater than or equal to 0.

datadog_logs_index.exclusion_filters.filter: The filter object defines the query criteria that determine which logs are excluded from the index based on the exclusion filter's configuration.
datadog_logs_index.exclusion_filters.filter.query: The query string to filter logs that should be excluded from the index. It follows the Datadog log search syntax.
datadog_logs_index.exclusion_filters.filter.sample_rate: The fraction of logs matching the exclusion filter query that will be excluded. Must be a number between 0 and 1, where 1.0 excludes all matching logs.
datadog_logs_index.exclusion_filters.is_enabled: Whether the exclusion filter is enabled. When true, logs matching the filter's query are excluded from the index.
datadog_logs_index.exclusion_filters.name: Name of the exclusion filter. This is a user-defined label used to identify the filter within the logs index.

datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.binary_to_text_encoding: Specifies the encoding used to convert binary data to text. Allowed values are `base64` and `base16`.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.categories: List of categories for the category processor. Each category contains a name and a filter query, and logs matching the query are assigned the corresponding category name.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.categories.filter: The filter object for this category, containing the log query used to match logs. Logs that match this query are assigned to this category.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.categories.filter.query: The query string used to filter logs into this category within the Datadog logs pipeline category processor.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.default_lookup: Default value to assign to the target attribute when the source field is not found in the lookup table.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.filter: This object defines the filter for the processor, including the query that matches logs and whether the processor is enabled. It contains a required `query` string and an optional `is_enabled` boolean.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.filter.query: The query string that defines which logs pass through this filter processor. It uses Datadog's log query syntax.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.grok: Configures the Grok parser processor, which uses Grok rules to extract structured data from raw log messages.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.grok.match_rules: The grok match rules, specified as a string containing one or more patterns separated by newlines, used to parse logs in the processor.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.grok.support_rules: Support rules for the Grok processor. These are named patterns that can be referenced by the main matching rules to build complex parsing logic.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.input_representation: Specifies the representation of the input data: `utf_8` for treating the input as UTF-8 encoded text, or `integer` for treating it as an integer value.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.is_enabled: Whether the processor is enabled. Set to false to disable the processor while keeping its configuration intact.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.is_replace_missing: Boolean flag indicating whether the lookup processor should replace the source attribute with the target value when the source attribute is missing. Set to true to enable replacement of missing source attributes.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.lookup_enrichment_table: The name of the enrichment table used by the lookup processor to enrich log data.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.lookup_table: List of strings that define the lookup table for the lookup processor. Each entry is a comma-separated mapping in the format 'source_value,target_value', used to replace or enrich attribute values.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers: A list of mapping rules for the attribute mapper processor, where each mapper remaps a source attribute to a target attribute with a specified type.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.categories.filter: The filter object for a category, containing the log query that determines whether a log entry is assigned to this category.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.categories.filter.que: The query string used to match logs for this category.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.categories.name: The name of the category. When the associated filter matches, the log is assigned this category.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.fallback.values: A map of strings that defines the fallback value mapping for the mapper processor. When the source attribute value does not match any of the primary mapper rules, this map is used to look up the corresponding target value.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.override_on_conflict: Whether to overwrite the target attribute when it already has a value. If false, the existing value is preserved and the mapping does not take effect.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.preserve_source: Preserves the original source attribute in the log after the remapping is applied. If false, the source attribute is removed after mapping.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.target: The name of the target attribute in the log that the mapped source value is written into. This is the new attribute that will be set with the value from the source attribute.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.target_format: Specifies the target data type for the mapped value. Allowed values are: auto, string, integer, double.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.mappers.type: The type of the mapper, which is 'schema-remapper' in this case. A schema remapper applies a schema mapping to logs, changing field names to align with a standard schema (e.g., remapping custom attributes to Datadog standard attributes).
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.normalize_ending_slashes: When set to `true`, this setting removes the trailing slash from the path of URLs handled by the URL parser processor (e.g., `http://example.com/path/` becomes `http://example.com/path`). When `false`, the URL remains unchanged.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.operation.filter: The Groq query used to filter logs that this processor operates on. When omitted, the processor applies to all logs.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.operation.override_on_conflic: Boolean that indicates whether the processor should overwrite an existing target attribute value when a conflict occurs. When set to true, the existing value is replaced; when set to false, the original value is kept.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.operation.preserve_source: Whether to preserve the source attribute after the operation is applied. When set to false, the source attribute is removed from the log.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.operation.target: The target log attribute name for the processor operation. This is the attribute that will be created or modified.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.override_on_conflict: Determines whether the processor overwrites an existing value on the target attribute when a conflict arises. Set to true to override the existing value, or false to preserve it.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.preserve_source: Whether to preserve the source attribute after remapping. When set to `true`, the original source attribute is retained; when `false`, it is removed.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.processors: A list of processors to apply to logs in this pipeline. Each processor defines a specific transformation, such as parsing or attribute remapping.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.samples: List of sample log messages used to validate the grok parser processor's rule. Each string in the list is an example log that the parser rule is tested against.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.schema.schema_type: Defines the scope of schema inference for the schema processor. Accepted values are 'full' (infer the schema of the entire log event) and 'attribute' (infer the schema of a specific attribute).
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.schema.version: The version of the processor schema. This value determines the schema version used to interpret the processor's configuration fields.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.source: The source attribute of the log event that this processor operates on (e.g., 'message').
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.sources: List of source attribute paths that the processor reads from. Used in remapper processors (e.g., attribute, date, message, service, status) to specify which log attributes are mapped to a target field.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.target: The name of the target log attribute that the processor operates on. This is the field in the log to which the processor applies its transformation or remapping.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.target_format: The format of the target value. Allowed values are `auto`, `string`, `integer`, and `double`.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.template: The template string used to generate a new attribute value, allowing references to other log attributes with the {{ attribute }} syntax.
datadog_logs_pipeline.processors.type: The type of processor. For this resource, the only allowed value is `grok-parser`, which indicates a Grok parser processor that extracts custom fields from log messages using Grok patterns.

datadog_monitor.assets.category: The category of the asset. Allowed value: `runbook`.
datadog_monitor.assets.resource_type: The type of the asset associated with the monitor. The only supported value is 'notebook'.
datadog_monitor.matching_downtimes.end: The timestamp (epoch seconds) when the downtime ends.
datadog_monitor.matching_downtimes.id: The unique identifier of the Datadog downtime that matches the monitor.
datadog_monitor.matching_downtimes.scope: The list of monitor scopes (such as host, service, or environment tags) to which the matching downtime applies. The downtime mutes monitors that match these scopes.
datadog_monitor.matching_downtimes.start: The start time of the matching downtime, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.
datadog_monitor.options.scheduling_options.custom_schedu: The RRULE expression, in RFC 5545 format, that defines the recurrence pattern for the custom schedule. For example, 'FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=2'.
The IANA timezone in which the recurrence's start and end times are expressed.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.aggregator: The aggregation method used for the variable query. Valid values are avg, sum, max, min, last, area, l2norm, percentile, stddev.
The alias for the column, used to reference the column in the monitor's template variables and messages.
The name of the column to be added to the augmented query result.
The time interval in seconds over which the compute aggregation is applied.
The name of the metric to use in the compute operation for the augmented query variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.augment_query.group_by: The facet used to group query results within the monitor's variable augment query. It specifies the field by which the query is grouped.
The maximum number of groups to return from the group_by operation in the augment query.
This object specifies the sorting parameters for the groups created by the group_by, controlling their display order in the monitor.
The aggregation method for the sort metric.
The metric name used to sort the groups in the augment query's group_by, combined with the aggregation and order to determine the sort order. For example, a metric like 'system.cpu.user'.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.augment_query.indexes: A list of log index names used by the augment query to restrict the scope of the variable's search. If not specified, the query may use all available indexes.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.augment_query.name: The name of the augment query, used to identify it within the monitor.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.augment_query.query_fi: The filter expression for the augment query.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.augment_query.search.q: The search query used to augment a monitor variable. It specifies the query string that defines what data to include in the augmentation search.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.aggregator: The aggregation method applied to the variable's base query, controlling how values are combined.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.compute: The compute object specifies the aggregation function and field used to transform the base query into a numeric value for the monitor variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.compute.agg: Defines the aggregation method (e.g., avg, sum, min, max, count) applied to the selected facet when computing the variable's value.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.compute.int: The time interval in seconds for the aggregation computation, e.g., 60 for per-minute intervals.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.compute.met: The metric name to apply the aggregation to in this compute operation (e.g., 'system.cpu.user').
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.data_source: The data source type for a monitor template variable, which determines where the variable's values are queried from (e.g., 'metrics', 'logs', 'rum', 'events').
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.group_by: A list of group-by definitions that determine the tag or attribute keys used to aggregate the base query results when populating the template variable's available values.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.group_by.fa: The tag or attribute name used to group query results in the monitor variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.group_by.li: The maximum number of groups to return for this group-by in the monitor variable's base query.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.group_by.so: The aggregation method applied to the metric when sorting grouped results, such as 'sum', 'avg', 'min', or 'max'.
The metric name used to sort the grouped results in the monitor variable's query, for example 'system.cpu.user'.
The sort order for the group by, either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.indexes: The list of log index names to search in the base query. If omitted, all log indexes are searched.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.name: The name of the template variable defined for the monitor. This name is used to reference the variable in the monitor's query or message.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.query: The base query string that defines the possible values for this template variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.base_query.search.quer: The search query string used to filter and populate the available values for the template variable. It defines the scope of events or data used to determine the possible variable values.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.compute: The compute block specifies the aggregation and facet used to calculate the value of the variable. It contains an `aggregation` field (required) and an optional `facet` field.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.compute.aggregation: Aggregation method applied to the compute variable. Valid values are: count, cardinality, median, pc75, pc90, pc95, pc98, pc99, sum, min, max, avg.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.compute.interval: The time interval (in seconds) over which the compute aggregation is evaluated. For example, a value of 300 represents a 5-minute window.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.compute.metric: The name of the metric to use for the computation.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.compute.source: The source of the variable's data. Valid values are `event`, `log`, `metric`, `process`, `rum`, `security`, and `trace`. Defaults to `metric`.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.data_source: The data source type for the monitor variable. Allowed values are: rum, ci_pipelines, ci_tests, audit, events, logs, spans, database_queries, network, network_path.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter: The filter query that restricts the possible values for this template variable in a Datadog monitor.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query: The filter query used to restrict the available values for this monitor template variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.columns.a: The alias for the column in the filter query, used as the display name in the Datadog monitor template variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.columns.n: The display name for a column in the filter query's columns list. This column is part of the monitor variable's filter query definition.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.compute: The compute block specifies the aggregation and, optionally, the interval applied to the filter query that generates the values for the monitor variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.compute.a: The aggregation function to apply when computing the variable, such as 'avg', 'sum', 'min', 'max', or 'count'.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.compute.i: The time interval, in seconds, used when computing the query aggregation.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.compute.m: The metric name to use for the compute aggregation in a filter query variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.data_sour: The data source type for the filter query, which determines the kind of Datadog data used to populate the monitor template variable. Accepts values such as `metrics`, `logs`, `rum`, `rum_issues`, `ci_pipelines`, `ci_tests`, `cloud_cost`, and `events`.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.group_by: List of objects defining how to group the values of this monitor variable. Each object represents one grouping (typically by a tag path) and can include a display label.
The facet (tag or attribute) to group by when filtering the variable's query, such as 'service' or 'host'.
The maximum number of groups to return for the variable's group_by query. Limits the number of choices available for the variable in the monitor's dashboard.
The aggregation method used to compute the sort value for the group-by in this filter query. For example, 'sum' or 'avg'.
The metric used to sort the grouped results in the variable's filter query.
The sort direction for the grouped results. Allowed values are 'asc' (ascending) and 'desc' (descending).
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.indexes: List of log index names to filter the query.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.name: The name of the template variable, used to reference the variable in the monitor message.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.query_fil: The query used to filter the available values for the template variable, limiting the variable's options to those that match the query.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filter_query.search.qu: The search query string used to filter results for this filter_query.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filters: Filters for the template variable, restricting the available values based on tag keys and values.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filters.base_attribute: The base attribute name used to filter the values available for the monitor variable. For example, when the filter's data source is 'logs', this could be a log facet like '@http.url'.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filters.exclude: Whether the filter is an exclusion filter. When true, the specified tag values are excluded from the template variable's available values.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.filters.filter_attribu: The attribute name that the filter uses to narrow the template variable's available values.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.group_by: List of grouping conditions for the monitor variable. Each item contains a name and tag used to group the query results when resolving the variable's value.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.group_by.facet: The facet (e.g., a tag key or attribute name) to group by for this monitor template variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.group_by.limit: The maximum number of groups to return for this group-by clause.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.group_by.sort: Sorting settings for the groups returned by this variable. It defines how the groups are ordered, such as ascending or descending.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.group_by.sort.aggregat: The aggregation method used to compute the sort value for group-by results. Allowed values are: count, cardinality, median, pc75, pc90, pc95, pc98, pc99, sum, min, max, avg.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.group_by.sort.metric: The name of the metric used to sort the group results in the Datadog monitor variable group-by sort condition.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.group_by.sort.order: Specifies the sort order for the group-by variable: 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.indexes: A list of log indexes that this template variable will be restricted to. When set, the variable only uses these indexes when querying log data in log-based monitors.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.jobs_query: The query used to populate the list of values for this monitor variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.join_condition.base_at: The attribute from the base query used to join with the other query in the join condition.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.join_condition.join_ty: The type of join to perform for the join condition. Valid values are 'inner' and 'left'.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.monitor_options: The options object for a monitor template variable. It contains a `values` attribute (a list of strings) that restricts the selectable values for the variable.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.monitor_options.custom: A custom where clause used to filter the available values for the monitor template variable. For example, you can scope the variable by specifying a tag-based filter like 'availability-zone:us-east-1a'.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.monitor_options.group_: A list of columns to group by for the variable's expression in the monitor query.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.monitor_options.model_: Override the model type for the monitor variable. Allowed values are 'freshness', 'percentage', or 'any'.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.monitor_options.sensit: The sensitivity of the anomaly detection monitor, from 1 (least sensitive) to 5 (most sensitive). This controls the width of the anomaly detection band.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.name: The name of the variable, which serves as the identifier used in the monitor's query or message for template variable substitution.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.query: The query string that defines the set of values for this monitor variable. It is used to populate the variable's available values, for example with a metric query or a list of hosts.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.query_dialect: The query language used for the variable's query. Valid values are `datadog` (default) for Datadog query syntax or `prometheus` for PromQL.
datadog_monitor.options.variables.search.query: The search query string used to filter the values available for this monitor variable.
datadog_monitor.state.groups.last_nodata_ts: Unix timestamp of the last time the monitor group reported no data.
datadog_monitor.state.groups.last_notified_ts: The timestamp of the last notification sent for this monitor group.
datadog_monitor.state.groups.last_resolved_ts: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the monitor group was last resolved.
datadog_monitor.state.groups.last_triggered_ts: The timestamp (Unix epoch) when the monitor last triggered an alert for this group.
datadog_monitor.state.groups.name: The name of the monitor group, typically the combination of tag values that defines the group for multi-alert monitors.

datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.cells.attributes.time.li: Boolean flag indicating whether the time range is live (auto-refreshing) as opposed to a fixed time range.

datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.cells.attributes.time.st: The start timestamp of the time range for the notebook cell, represented as a string (e.g., ISO 8601 format).
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.cells.type: The type of notebook cell. The only allowed value is "notebook_cells".
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.template_variables.avail: The list of possible values that can be assigned to the template variable in a Datadog notebook.

datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.template_variables.data_: A map from data source types (e.g., 'metrics', 'logs') to template variable values, allowing the variable to resolve to different values depending on the data source used by a panel.
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.template_variables.defau: The default value for the template variable, used when no other value is selected.

datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.template_variables.name: The name of the template variable, used to reference it in notebook queries.
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.template_variables.prefi: The text prefix that is prepended to the template variable's value when used in notebook queries. For example, a prefix of 'env:' with a selected value of 'prod' would produce 'env:prod'.
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.template_variables.type: The type of the template variable, either 'tag' for tag keys or 'host' for host names.
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.time.end: The end of the timeframe for the notebook. This is part of the time attribute that specifies the range of data shown.
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.time.live: Whether the notebook time range is live (updates automatically) rather than a fixed range.
datadog_notebook_response.data.attributes.time.start: The start time of the notebook's time range, in ISO 8601 format.

datadog_shared_dashboard.invitees.email: The email address of the invitee granted access to the shared dashboard.

datadog_shared_dashboard.selectable_template_vars.name: The name of the template variable that will be selectable by viewers of the shared dashboard. Must correspond to a template variable defined on the dashboard.

datadog_shared_dashboard.selectable_template_vars.visible_tags: List of tag values that are shown as selectable options for this template variable in the shared dashboard.

datadog_sloresponse.data.sli_specification.count.bad_events_: The formula string used to define the count of bad events for the SLI, such as a Datadog query or mathematical expression.
datadog_sloresponse.data.sli_specification.count.good_events: Block defining a formula used to compute the good events count for a count-based SLI specification. This is used in place of a simple query when good events are derived from a formula.

datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.config_variables.pattern: Regular expression pattern used to generate random values for the config variable during test execution.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.config_variables.secure: Whether the config variable is a secure (hidden) variable. When set to true, the variable's value is not displayed in the UI or API responses.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.config_variables.type: The type of configuration variable. Allowed values are: `global`, `text`, `email`.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.access_token_u: The URL used to obtain an OAuth access token during authentication for the synthetic request.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.add_claims: Map of custom claims to add to the authentication request, where each key is the claim name and the corresponding value is the claim value.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.add_claims.iat: If true, includes the 'issued at' (iat) claim in the JWT token used for basic authentication.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.audience: The audience for the OAuth2 token, used when the basic auth type is set to 'oauth2'.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.client_secret: The client secret used for OAuth client authentication in the request's basic_auth configuration.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.domain: The domain for NTLM authentication in the basic auth configuration. Used when the auth type is set to 'ntlm'.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.password: The password to use for basic authentication against the requested endpoint.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.region: The AWS region to use for SigV4 authentication. Only relevant when the basic authentication type is set to `sigv4`.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.secret: The password or secret used for basic authentication against the endpoint.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.service_name: The service name to use for NTLM authentication within the basic auth configuration.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.token_prefix: The prefix (scheme) to prepend to the token in the Authorization header, e.g., 'Bearer'.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.type: The type of basic authentication to use for the request.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.username: The username used for basic authentication in the Synthetics browser test request.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.basic_auth.workstation: The workstation name for NTLM authentication.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.files.bucket_key: The object key (path) of the file within the S3 bucket to be uploaded for the browser test.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.files.content: The base64-encoded content of the file to be uploaded in the browser test request. The maximum length of the string is 3,145,728 characters (3 MB).
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.files.encoding: Encoding of the file content, such as 'base64'.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.files.name: The name of the file to be sent in the request, used as the filename in multipart form data. Must be at most 1500 characters.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.files.original_file_name: The original filename of the file to be uploaded in the browser test step. Must be a string with a maximum length of 1500 characters.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.files.size: The size of the file, in bytes. The value must be between 1 and 3,145,728 bytes (3 MB).
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.request.files.type: The MIME type (content type) of the uploaded file, such as 'application/json' or 'image/png'. Must be at most 1500 characters.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.variables.example: The example value for the variable.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.variables.name: The name of the variable, used to reference this variable in the browser test configuration.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.variables.pattern: Regular expression pattern used to generate random values for the variable.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.variables.secure: Set to true to mark the variable as secure, preventing its value from being displayed in test results and logs.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.config.variables.type: The type of the variable used in the browser test. Valid values are `element`, `email`, `global`, and `text`.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.options.scheduling.timeframes.day: The day of the week (1=Monday, 7=Sunday) that this timeframe applies to.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.options.scheduling.timeframes.from: The start time of the scheduling timeframe, formatted as HH:mm in 24-hour time.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.options.scheduling.timeframes.to: The end time of the scheduling time window.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.allow_failure: When set to true, failures in this step are allowed and do not fail the entire test. This is useful for steps that may be conditional or non-critical.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.always_execute: Boolean that indicates whether the step should always be executed, even if a previous step fails. If set to false, the step will be skipped when a preceding step fails.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.exit_if_succeed: If set to `true`, the test stops and is marked as successful when this step succeeds. Defaults to `false`.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.is_critical: Whether the step is critical. If set to `true`, a failure of this step causes the entire synthetic test to fail. If `false`, the step can fail without failing the test. Defaults to `false`.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.no_screenshot: When set to true, screenshots are not taken for this step.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.params: A dynamic object containing step-specific configuration, such as the element to interact with, text to input, or assertion details, depending on the step type in a Datadog synthetic browser test.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.timeout: The maximum time, in milliseconds, to wait for the step to complete before failing.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test.steps.type: The type of step in the browser test, determining the action to be performed. Allowed values include click, typeText, hover, wait, assertCurrentUrl, assertElementPresent, and others.

datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.config.variables.example: Sample value for the variable, used as an example in the test configuration.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.config.variables.name: The name of the variable, used to reference it within the test configuration.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.config.variables.secure: Whether the variable is a secure variable, meaning its value is encrypted and hidden in the UI.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.config.variables.type: The type of the Synthetics mobile test variable. Valid values are `global` (references a global variable), `text` (a literal text value), and `email` (a generated email address).
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.options.bindings.principals: List of principals (users, groups, or roles) that this binding applies to. Each principal is a string identifier such as a user email or a group ID.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.options.bindings.relation: The type of access granted to the bound role. Allowed values are `editor` (full edit access) and `viewer` (read-only access).
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.options.scheduling.timeframes.day: The day of the week for this scheduling timeframe, where 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Must be between 1 and 7.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.options.scheduling.timeframes.from: Start time of the time frame during which the test is scheduled to run.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.options.scheduling.timeframes.to: The end time of the scheduling timeframe, formatted as HH:MM.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.allow_failure: Determines if the mobile test step can fail without marking the entire test as failed. When set to true, a failure in this step will not fail the overall test.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.is_critical: A boolean indicating whether this step is critical. If a critical step fails, the entire test is considered failed; non-critical steps do not cause failure on their own.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.name: The name of the step in the Datadog Synthetics mobile test. Must be at most 1500 characters.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.no_screenshot: Whether to disable the screenshot capture for this step. Set to true to prevent Datadog from taking a screenshot during this step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.check: The type of check to perform on the target value. Allowed values: equals, notEquals, contains, notContains, startsWith, notStartsWith, greater, lower, greaterEquals, lowerEquals, matchRegex, between, isEmpty, notIsEmpty.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.delay: Delay in milliseconds to wait before executing the step. Must be between 0 and 5000.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.direction: Specifies the direction of the mobile gesture (e.g., swipe), with allowed values: up, down, left, right.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.context_type: Specifies whether the element is in a native or web context. Allowed values are 'native' and 'web'.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.element_description: A description of the mobile UI element targeted by the step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.multi_locator: A list of alternative locators for the element, allowing the synthetics mobile test to use any of these locators to find the element during test execution.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.relative_position.x: The x-coordinate of the element's relative position within the parent context, used to define the element's location for interaction in the mobile test step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.relative_position.y: The y-coordinate of the element's relative position, used to define the vertical offset from the reference element.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.text_content: The text content of the on-screen element used to identify and interact with it in the mobile test step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.user_locator.fail_t: If true, the mobile test step is marked as failed when the specified user locator fails to locate the element.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.user_locator.values: The type of locator used to identify a mobile element. Allowed values: accessibility-id, id, ios-predicate-string, ios-class-chain, xpath.
A single string value in the user locator 'values' list, used to identify the mobile element during the test step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.element.view_name: The name of the view (screen) in the mobile application where the element is located.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.max_scrolls: The maximum number of scroll actions to perform during this mobile test step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.positions.x: The x-coordinate (horizontal position) of the point on the screen, in pixels.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.positions.y: The y-coordinate of the position, representing the vertical location on the screen.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.subtest_public_id: The public ID of the subtest to run in this step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.value: The value associated with a parameter for a step in the mobile test. The type is dynamic and can vary based on the specific step and parameter.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.with_enter: Whether to press the Enter key after inputting text in the step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.params.x: The horizontal (x) coordinate for the interaction point in the mobile test step.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test.steps.type: The type of step to perform in the mobile test. Possible values include assertElementContent, assertScreenContains, assertScreenLacks, doubleTap, extractVariable, flick, openDeeplink, playSubTest, pressBack, restartApplication, rotate, scroll, scrollToElement, tap, toggleWiFi, typeText, and wait.
